subject: Quantitative Reasoning
introduction: Work and Rate problems involve people or machines completing tasks. Key idea: if someone finishes a job in n days, their rate = 1/n of the job per day. Combine rates by adding. Master LCM method for clean integer solutions.
tips_and_tricks: LCM method: set total work = LCM of all time values. Compute each rate as work/time.
Combined rate = sum of individual rates. Time = Total Work / Combined rate.
Pipe problems: filling pipes add, emptying pipes subtract.
If A is twice as fast as B: A's time = half of B's time.
Remaining work problems: work done first + work done together = 1.
MDH formula: M×D×H = constant work. Useful for problems with varying workers/hours.

worked_examples.title: Example 1: Two workers together
worked_examples.question: A can do a job in 6 days, B in 12 days. How long do they take together?
solution: LCM method: LCM(6,12)=12. A does 2/day, B does 1/day. Together: 3/day. 12/3 = 4 days ✓

worked_examples.title: Example 2: Filling tank with leak
worked_examples.question: A pipe fills a tank in 4h. A leak empties it in 12h. How long to fill with the leak?

questions.subject: Quantitative Reasoning
questions.question_text: A pump fills a pool in 6h. A drain empties it in 9h. Pool is 2/3 full. How long to fully empty with only drain open, then drain+pump both open?

options.text: Drain only=6h to empty 2/3; both open=18h to empty remaining
Drain only: 9h to empty all; both: never empty

questions.explanation:
Drain only empties 2/3 of pool: time to empty 2/3 = (2/3)×9h = 6h.

With both open: net rate = -1/9+1/6 = -2/18+3/18 = 1/18 fill rate (POSITIVE). Tank fills, doesn't empty when both open.
hints: With both open: net=1/6-1/9=(3-2)/18=1/18 fill rate.
Both open fills the tank — it won't empty.
